title: Literature check: c40's dividing CIPS condensates are a variant of Zwicker et al. 2017 and Demarchi et al. 2023 (enzyme condensates that divide and self-propel); Froese-Ikegami-Virgo's parasitic autocatalyst is a route to IXDE
summary: Opened 4 primary sources. c40's SIED result (CIPS condensates from noise that divide repeatedly on a consumed fuel) uses Zwicker et al.'s growth-then-shape-instability division, and Demarchi et al. 2023 already report division, arrested coarsening and self-propulsion of enzyme condensates driven by their own catalysis; the new part is spontaneous formation, fuel dependence shown by fork and local cut, and repeated generations. Two ideas: a parasitic autocatalyst on the condensates (Froese, Ikegami and Virgo 2012) for C:ecology-with-reproduction, and Demarchi's propulsion threshold in c40's world for swimming, dividing, metabolic condensates.

sources.cite: Zwicker, Seyboldt, Weber, Hyman & Jülicher 2017, Nat Phys 13:408
sources.note: chemically active droplets grow on reaction-made material and divide by a shape instability; the mechanism of c40's division

enzyme-enriched condensates: catalysis-driven enzyme fluxes give interrupted coarsening, equidistant positioning, division, and self-propulsion above a feedback threshold; the nearest model to c40's world
catalysis-induced phase separation, the parent class

sources.cite: Froese, Ikegami & Virgo 2012, ALIFE 13 (MIT Press), The behavior-based hypercycle
sources.note: a parasitic autocatalyst C (B + 2C -> 3C) on Gray-Scott spots: spots flee, the parasite follows as a tail; spots eat food and divide. A predator operator for IXDE

prior_art.note: division and arrested coarsening of enzyme condensates are published; spontaneous nucleation, fuel dependence by fork and local cut, and repeated generations are what c40 adds; mechanism as Zwicker et al. 2017
